loss_reason: Closed-lost — customer decided to build/operate their own stack (vLLM + TGI on k8s with TensorRT-LLM for NVIDIA fleet). Primary drivers: long-term unit-cost, strict PHI residency, and ops control. Secondary: internal procurement freeze and no clear exec champion to pay hosted premium.
notes:
Status: Closed-lost (internal). Summary: Ironwood validated Redwood Dedicated during PoC (latency OK, Stable tokens), but after infosec deep-dive they concluded corporate policy mandates customer-managed key material + air-gapped capability for certain workloads. Ops team pushed for full control over quantization/FP16 pipelines — insisted on TensorRT optimizations for their on-prem A100/Tesla fleet. Quote from CTO: "We can't accept per-token variability at enterprise scale — need deterministic unit economics and full stack control."

POC highlights: quick integration with SDK, streaming worked, but cost projections vs. 3-yr self-host TCO favored self-hosting once infra amortization included. Customer ran a baseline with vLLM + TGI (community) and saw comparable throughput once TensorRT kernels were integrated.

Internal dynamics: procurement put a freeze Nov 2025 after org-wide cost-reduction directive. No single product owner to escalate license/commit. Sales attempts: pricing concession and dedicated pilot offered; security team asked for HSM integration, SCIM/SAML audit, and on-prem deployment package — timeline >9 months.

Recommended next steps for Redwood: 1) Mark as closed-lost with detailed loss-reason tags; 2) Add to private-deploy partnership list (potential SI for deployment automation); 3) Re-engage in 6-9 months for hybrid/offload use-case (cold-cache or reranking to hosted) and to surface potential Migrate-from-self-host program.
